newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh leader strengthens economic ministries.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader strengthens economic ministries.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev is strengthening economic ministries in a plan to slim down the unwieldy and inefficient government apparatus.
"The sharp reduction of the apparatus is the strongest blow to corruption, bribe-taking and irresponsibility," Nazarbayev told a news conference on Tuesday.

In line with a decree published in the official Kazakhstanskaya Pravda daily paper on Wednesday, the number of ministries, committees and other state bodies in the former Soviet republic is being reduced to 25 from 47. Several key economic ministries have been given larger powers.

Economy Minister Umirzak Shukeyev becomes Minister of Economy and Trade, with his department absorbing the ministries of economy, industry and commerce, building as well as the state committees on prices, anti-monopoly policy and statistics.

Energy and Coal Industry Minister Viktor Khrapunov heads a new expanded Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources, which takes over the ministries of energy and coal industry, oil and gas, and geology.
The Oil and Gas Ministry is being replaced by a national company called Kazakh Oil, which will manage and own a stake in Western energy deals.
Former Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev was appointed head of the national oil company.
Nazarbayev said on Tuesday Kazakh Oil would have a 40 to 50 percent stake in all joint ventures and all companies under Western management which are developing Kazakh oil reserves.
Kazakhstan's biggest energy investment is the $20 billion Tengiz project by Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp, both of the United States.
Nazarbayev's decree dissolves the State Privatisation and the State Property Committees, the State Tax Committee and some other bodies, whose functions passed to the Finance Ministry.
Nazarbayev also set up agencies for Control of Strategic Resources and for Strategic Planning which will report directly to him, but their future functions remain unclear.
